content.value_statement: React Native projects can become difficult to maintain when component, state, and asynchronous patterns vary between features. This skill provides focused examples for choosing consistent, readable implementation patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows custom hook, compound component, and render prop patterns.
Explains when to use local state, React Context, or Zustand.
Provides a cancellable async data-fetching hook example.
Demonstrates memoization and React lazy loading patterns.
Includes error boundary, safe area, and keyboard handling examples.
limitations: Provides patterns and examples, not a complete application architecture.
Does not configure libraries, dependencies, or build tooling.
Examples may require adaptation for a project API and React Native version.
Does not replace performance profiling or automated testing.

use_cases.title: Build a reusable screen feature
use_cases.description: Choose a component and state pattern before implementing a new mobile screen.

use_cases.title: Refactor an existing feature
use_cases.description: Break a large component into focused hooks, providers, and child components.

use_cases.title: Review implementation choices
use_cases.description: Compare data fetching, cleanup, and error handling against documented practices.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a state pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a React Native settings screen. Recommend local state, Context, or Zustand and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Extract a custom hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Native component and propose a custom hook for its reusable state and side-effect logic.

prompt_templates.title: Improve data fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor my React Native user data request to handle loading, errors, cancellation, and component cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a focused refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this large React Native screen. Create a refactor plan using component boundaries, state ownership, error handling, and performance measurements.

output_examples.input: Which state solution should a shared theme use?
output: Recommendation: React Context for a cross-cutting theme value.
Reason: Theme state is shared broadly but changes infrequently.
Next step: Create a provider and a typed useTheme hook.

output_examples.input: How should a user profile request handle unmounting?
output: Use a cleanup flag or request cancellation in the effect cleanup function.
Update state only while the component remains active.
Expose data, loading, and error states to the screen.

best_practices: Keep components focused on one responsibility and extract reusable logic into hooks.
Model loading, error, and empty states before connecting a screen to an API.
Profile real performance bottlenecks before adding memoization or lazy loading.
anti_patterns: Do not put unrelated state, requests, and rendering logic in one large component.
Do not update component state after an asynchronous request has been cleaned up.
Do not introduce global state when local state or Context is sufficient.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers React Native patterns for components, state, data fetching, performance, errors, and mobile layout concerns.

faq.question: Does this skill write a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It supplies focused patterns that you adapt to your project requirements.

faq.question: When should I use Zustand?
faq.answer: Use it for app-wide state that is not well served by local component state or a focused Context provider.

faq.question: Does it include API integration?
faq.answer: It includes a relative API fetching example, but it does not configure an API client or backend.

faq.question: Will memoization always improve performance?
faq.answer: No. Measure performance first because unnecessary memoization can add complexity.

faq.question: Can I use these patterns in an existing app?
faq.answer: Yes. Use them to guide incremental refactoring while preserving your project conventions.
